title: How products are displayed
summary: Two shops can sell the same item and look nothing alike: Supermarket Simulator gives products a display type and keeps product data with the crates they arrive in.
body: A product carries a display type of its own, which is why the game can decide how something is meant to be shown rather than leaving it entirely to you.
Crates carry product data with them, so what is in a box is known to the game before you open it rather than discovered afterwards.
Because a product keeps its own identifier, how it is displayed is a property of that product rather than a setting on one shelf.
What this entry does not tell you: how many display types exist or which one sells best. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Products carry a display type of their own.
Crates carry product data with them.
Each product keeps its own identifier, independent of any shelf.
The build ships both a metal and a wooden pegboard display, each with a material of its own.
Display pieces for particular counters are shipped as well, a deli one and a single-width bakery one among them.
Taking a product off a shelf is animated at three heights, each with a loop of its own.
facts.evidence: asset names: Take_Product_High, Take_Product_Mid, Take_Product_Low, Take_Product_High_Loop, Take_Product_Low_Loop
